# Pinned WebRTC async driver

Imported library sources from crates.io `webrtc` version 0.21.1, whose packaged
VCS metadata records commit `d658b5a803dd8dc389547450e245877310c9cbed` from
https://github.com/webrtc-rs/webrtc. No upstream submission is made by this fork.

The downloaded crate archive was verified against the registry lock checksum:
`b621e736302bef784948cc8d8099fd0a8fdb5757693c80a344ffbe38c49387d2`.
MIT and Apache licenses are preserved verbatim. This copy includes `src`, the
normalized and original package manifests, README, licenses and VCS metadata. Example and
integration-test target declarations are omitted because those targets are not
vendored. Numeric GitHub issue references in source comments use bare numbers
to comply with this fork's reference policy. Production dependencies and their
version constraints are unchanged. Defaults remain disabled by the parent.

The maintained behavior changes include `peer_connection/driver.rs`:
drain pending TURN writes after draining core writes, before the driver waits
for another event. Core media can enqueue a relay datagram after the earlier
TURN drain; leaving that datagram queued makes an idle final frame wait for an
unrelated network or timer event. Also dispatch core events generated by TURN
decapsulation before draining media, so a remote track exists when its first
RTP packet is delivered. The direct read path already has that ordering.
Direct UDP/GSO behavior is unchanged. The
forced-relay tests in the parent media crate cover actual coturn transport.

`runtime/mod.rs` adds an optional, default-disabled TURN-only local-address
preference. `transport/turn_relayer.rs` evaluates it once per destination
family using actual bound sockets. The default keeps every interface, and
host/STUN gathering is unchanged. The embedding media wrapper prefers the
OS-selected UDP route only when it is available, otherwise preserving the
caller's explicit alternatives; its TCP/TLS IPC uses one binding per family.
Rebinding reevaluates the preference rather than reusing stale interface IPs.
The two-binding actual-coturn tests require one relay endpoint per peer and
retain both host candidates in automatic mode, followed by nominated media.

`Runtime::turn_gathering_delay` is a default-zero optional policy for incremental
ICE embedders. The existing driver timer schedules deferred TURN, never a sleep
inside the event handler; host/STUN, reads, DTLS, writes and Close remain live.
A Connected event cancels the deferred allocation and completes the TURN part
of gathering. If no connection exists at the deadline, normal TURN gathering
starts. Relay-only mode bypasses the grace; rebind clears stale deferred work.
The wrapper uses 250 ms only for Automatic trickle peers with configured TURN.
Full-SDP callers and the SDK default remain immediate. Actual-coturn fixtures
cover skipped native LAN allocations and delayed UDP/TCP/TLS fallback; a close
fixture requires no late Allocate after its original deadline.

When updating, verify the new package checksum, preserve licenses, reapply this
driver and optional interface changes and rerun the forced UDP/TCP/TLS relay fixtures. URL parsing,
loopback transport tests and native cross-compilation do not replace them.
